title: Transparent Tribe
summary: Transparent Tribe is a espionage cluster that public reporting associates with South Asian state interests and that has focused for years on military, government and educational targets, mainly in India and neighbouring countries. The group is known for a high rate of campaign activity and for lures built around recruitment, job offers and examinations, which it uses to deliver Android applications and Windows executables that impersonate legitimate tools. On the mobile side, reporting describes fake versions of popular messaging and meeting applications that request extensive permissions and provide persistent access to messages, contacts, files and location, while desktop activity has used document lures and self-extracting archives alongside backdoors and remote administration tools. The group has also been reported to compromise legitimate websites and use them to host payloads, which extends the lifetime of its infrastructure. Attribution statements in public reporting carry moderate confidence and the cluster is tracked under several names, so behaviour is the reliable indicator. Evidence includes application installation records on managed devices, unusual outbound connections from phones, and archive or document execution chains on endpoints.

beginner.definition: Transparent Tribe is a name used by researchers for a group that spies on military, government and university targets, mainly in South Asia. Public reports link it to interests in the region. It uses fake job and exam messages to deliver harmful apps.
beginner.whyItMatters: Job offers and exam notices are emotional and urgent, so people act quickly. This group builds its attacks around that reaction. Its mobile apps can read messages and files, which is a serious loss for anyone working with sensitive material. Because it also uses real websites to host its files, blocking a single address does not help for long.
howItWorks: The group writes a message about a job, a scholarship or an exam result.
It sends the message to many people who would care about that topic.
The message asks them to install an app to view details or join an interview.
The app is a copy of a real chat or meeting program with hidden code added.
It asks for wide permissions and then reads messages, files and location.
The group also hides files on real websites, so links keep working for a long time.
beginner.example: Imagine a notice board outside a university that says interview list posted inside. Students rush to the office and accept whatever paper they are handed, because the news is exciting. A criminal who understands that moment does not need to break a lock. They only need to stand where people are already hurrying, which is exactly what a fake job or exam lure does.
takeaways: Verify job and exam messages through the official website, never through the message link.
Use mobile device management to see which apps are installed on work phones.
Attackers host files on real websites, so judge the app, not just the domain.

objectives: Explain how recruitment and examination themes create urgency that defeats careful judgement.
Describe the mobile permissions that indicate an app is collecting private data.
Explain why hosting payloads on legitimate websites extends attacker infrastructure lifetime.
Identify endpoint evidence of a self-extracting archive or document execution chain.
State how publicly reported attribution for this cluster is qualified.
